meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9
meta.title: Entry Check: Vocabulary from Literature to Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: After a protagonist admits a mistake and rebuilds trust through repeated honest action, which theme is best supported by this development?
choices: Apology alone can often repair trust.
Fear can sometimes motivate honest behavior.
questions.explanation: Admitting the mistake and repeatedly acting honestly supports the theme that accountability can help restore trust.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In the word preview, what meaning does the prefix pre- contribute?
questions.explanation: The prefix pre- means before, so a preview presents something before its event or full release.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: A character moves to a new town, feels lonely at first, then joins a music club and forms lasting friendships. Which statement best expresses the theme of this development?
choices: Belonging can grow when people take part in a community.
Fame brings lasting happiness to those who pursue it.
New places are always dangerous for young people.
Music is more valuable than academic study.
questions.explanation: The character overcomes loneliness by joining a group and making friends, which supports the theme that belonging can grow through community participation.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: An advertisement says, Thousands of healthy people choose our cereal every morning, so you should choose it too. Which logical fallacy does the argument commit?
questions.explanation: The argument uses the popularity of a choice rather than evidence of its quality, making it an appeal to popularity.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In the word replay, what meaning does the prefix re- contribute?
questions.explanation: The prefix re- means again, so replay means to play something again.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains an example of onomatopoeia?
choices: The kettle whistled as the water began to boil.
The kettle sat on the stove until the water began to boil.
The kettle was silver and polished for many years.
The kettle was the first thing Maya bought for her new kitchen.
questions.explanation: Whistled imitates the sound a kettle makes, so the sentence is an example of onomatopoeia.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: An argument says, 'The school must either cancel every arts program or risk losing the community's support.' Which logical fallacy does the argument commit?
questions.explanation: The argument falsely reduces the available choices to canceling all arts programs or losing community support.
questions.topic: Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to candid?
questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and direct, so frank is its closest synonym.
questions.topic: Vocabulary from Literature

questions.prompt: A young inventor's first design fails during a school exhibition. After listening to visitors' comments, she revises the design, and the improved version helps several neighbors solve a daily problem. Which theme is best supported?
choices: Feedback can turn an early failure into useful progress.
Useful inventions are usually created without outside advice.
A public exhibition matters more than solving a practical problem.
Only the inventor's first design deserves public support.
questions.explanation: The story shows that using feedback after a failure can lead to a more useful design.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: An advertisement says a supplement is effective because a famous athlete uses it, but gives no research about the supplement. Which logical fallacy does the advertisement commit?
questions.explanation: The argument is an appeal to authority because it treats the athlete's fame and endorsement as proof instead of providing evidence about the supplement.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: Which word carries the most positive connotation for someone who faces danger without backing down?
questions.explanation: Courageous is a complimentary word for facing danger bravely, while the other choices carry negative meanings.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In the sentence The evidence was so compelling that the jury returned a verdict, what does compelling mean?
questions.explanation: Here, compelling means convincing and persuasive, describing evidence strong enough to support the jury's verdict.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains an understatement?
choices: The flood reached our first-floor windows with a hungry roar.
The flood reached our first-floor windows, which was a minor inconvenience.
The flood reached our first-floor windows before dawn.
The flood reached our first-floor windows in a dazzling silver sheet.
questions.explanation: Calling a first-floor flood a minor inconvenience deliberately downplays how serious the event is.
questions.topic: Literary Devices

questions.prompt: Which literary device appears in the sentence The old house groaned as the storm shook its windows?
questions.explanation: The house is given the human ability to groan, making the description personification.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: An argument says, The reading program is effective, so it deserves support; it deserves support, so it is effective. Which logical fallacy does the argument commit?
questions.explanation: The argument assumes that effectiveness justifies support and uses that support to prove effectiveness, making its reasoning circular.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: A teenager spends several evenings patiently showing an elderly neighbor how to use a video-call app, never rushing when the neighbor asks her to repeat a step. Which statement best expresses the theme suggested by this detail?
choices: Patient care can be a meaningful expression of kindness.
Video-call apps are designed mainly to replace in-person visits.
Older adults should be encouraged to avoid unfamiliar technology.
Teenagers are usually more responsible than older adults.
questions.explanation: The teenager's patient, repeated help presents kindness as care expressed through time and attention.
questions.skill: Identifying Theme from a Literary Detail
questions.topic: Theme in Literature

questions.prompt: Which word is the base word in unforgettable?
questions.explanation: In unforgettable, forget is the base word, with un- added as a prefix and -able added as a suffix.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: After reading about the coming storm, Rafael moved his grandfather's small boat to a sheltered dock. Which inference is best supported by this action?
choices: Rafael expected the storm to damage the boat.
Rafael wanted to sell the boat before the storm.
Rafael planned to use the boat during the storm.
Rafael forgot where the boat was kept.
questions.explanation: Moving the boat to shelter after a storm warning suggests that Rafael expected bad weather to threaten it.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: An argument says, 'I bought a new notebook, and my test scores improved, so the notebook made me a better student.' Which logical fallacy does the argument commit?
questions.explanation: The argument treats the notebook purchase as the cause of the higher scores even though other factors could explain the improvement.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In the sentence The novel's final chapter was anticlimactic, ending with a whisper instead of the dramatic confrontation readers expected, what does anticlimactic most nearly mean?
choices: lacking a satisfying or exciting ending
full of suspense and dramatic tension
questions.explanation: Anticlimactic means lacking a satisfying or exciting ending, which matches the quiet, undramatic ending described in the sentence.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'After hours of debate, the committee finally reached a consensus,' what does consensus mean?
choices: a decision made by the chair alone
a promise to debate the issue again
questions.explanation: Consensus means general agreement reached by a group after discussion.
questions.topic: Vocabulary from Literature

questions.prompt: One speaker says, 'The library should close on Sundays.' Another replies, 'That person wants libraries closed every day, leaving students nowhere to study.' Which fallacy does the reply use?
questions.explanation: The reply changes a proposal to close only on Sundays into a claim that the speaker wants all libraries closed every day, thereby distorting the position.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: The suffix -ful in beautiful contributes which meaning?
choices: having a quality in large measure
having a quality in small measure
being unable to have any quality
being likely to lose a quality
questions.explanation: The suffix -ful means full of something or having a quality in large measure.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: A reader says, 'The three novels on my shelf have weak plots, so every novel published this year has a weak plot.' Which logical fallacy does the argument commit?
questions.explanation: The argument jumps from the qualities of three novels to a sweeping conclusion about every novel published that year.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: Which point of view narrates a story with pronouns such as I, me, and my?
questions.explanation: First-person point of view uses pronouns such as I, me, and my to narrate events from a participant's perspective.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Narrative Point of View

questions.prompt: In which word does the prefix inter- mean between or among?
questions.explanation: The prefix inter- means between or among, and international describes something involving multiple nations.
questions.topic: Vocabulary from Literature

questions.prompt: In the sentence The exhausted climber clung to the ledge, what does exhausted most nearly mean?
choices: very tired and in need of rest
pleased to have reached the summit
eager to begin a harder climb
questions.explanation: Exhausted means extremely tired and in need of rest.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In the word readable, what meaning does the suffix -able contribute?
choices: not yet able to be read
questions.explanation: The suffix -able means capable of being, so -able in readable means capable of being read.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Word Parts

questions.prompt: A narrator notes that a character's hands tremble while she accepts a public award. Which inference is best supported?
choices: She feels nervous while receiving the honor.
She feels relieved as the ceremony ends.
She expects someone to challenge the award.
She wishes she had refused the honor.
questions.explanation: Trembling hands commonly indicate nervousness, supporting the inference that she feels nervous while receiving the honor.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: The word cheap can mean low in price, but in a review of a poorly made jacket it carries a negative connotation. What does connotation refer to?
choices: the emotional coloring or attitude a word carries
the literal dictionary definition of a word
the number of syllables in a word
the historical origin of a word
questions.explanation: Connotation is the emotional coloring or attitude a word carries beyond its literal dictionary meaning.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'Although the topic was complex, the author's lucid explanation made every step easy to follow,' what does lucid mean?
questions.explanation: Lucid means clear and easy to understand, which matches the explanation that readers could follow every step.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: A character says, 'I'm fine,' then turns away and avoids everyone. Which inference is best supported by this behavior?
choices: The character is certainly planning to leave the room.
The character may be feeling uneasy or upset.
The character dislikes every person nearby.
The character has already decided to tell the truth.
questions.explanation: Avoiding others after saying 'I'm fine' suggests possible discomfort, but it does not justify the stronger claims in the other choices.
questions.topic: Character Analysis

questions.prompt: Which term specifically names the repeated initial p sound in the line Peter paid the polite piper?
questions.explanation: Alliteration is the repetition of the same consonant sound at the beginning of successive words.
questions.topic: Sound Devices in Literature

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The meticulous detective recorded every detail of the crime scene,' what does meticulous mean?
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, so the detective is careful and precise.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In a novel Sam read, the order of events was so ____ that he reread the chapter three times and still could not identify the first major change. Which word best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Convoluted means complex and difficult to understand, which matches Sam's inability to follow the sequence of events.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9:

questions.prompt: Which story detail most directly supports the theme that steady effort can succeed over time?
choices: A student sells an instrument at a market near the school.
A student criticizes a band after hearing its first song.
A student abandons music when practice becomes difficult.
A student practices a difficult passage daily and gradually performs it confidently.
questions.explanation: The daily practice and gradual improvement show steady effort leading to success.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In the word 'endless,' what meaning does the suffix -less contribute?
questions.explanation: The suffix -less means without, so endless describes something that has no end.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: The narrator calls the abandoned garden a wilderness of weeds and tangled vines. Which word best explains wilderness in this context?
choices: a modest place with few visitors
questions.explanation: Here, wilderness describes an overgrown place where plants grow without order or care.
questions.topic: Vocabulary from Literature

questions.prompt: The sentence I have told you a million times! is an example of which figure of speech?
questions.explanation: The phrase exaggerates how often the speaker has repeated the message, making it hyperbole.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The desert was an ocean of sand,' which literary device is used?
questions.explanation: The sentence compares the desert to an ocean without using like or as, making it a metaphor.
questions.topic: Figurative Language

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses a literary theme?
choices: The story takes place in a coastal town during winter.
The central event is a package delivered to the wrong house.
The main character is a girl who is named Elena.
Trust can deepen when people face hardship together.
questions.explanation: A theme is a complete message about life, and trust deepening through hardship expresses such a message.
questions.topic: Themes in Literature

questions.prompt: A narrator describes a long-empty school gym as a cathedral of vanished cheers, making the building seem grand but painfully quiet. Which tone is best?
questions.explanation: The phrase vanished cheers and the description of painful quiet create a melancholy, reflective mood.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Tone in Literature

questions.prompt: In the word beneficial, what meaning does the prefix bene- contribute?
questions.explanation: The prefix bene- means good, as in a beneficial outcome that is helpful or favorable.
questions.skill: Using a Prefix to Determine Meaning
questions.topic: Word Parts in Literature

questions.prompt: An argument says, 'If the school allows one student to redo an assignment, soon every student will redo every assignment and no one will turn in original work.' Which fallacy does this argument commit?
questions.explanation: The argument claims one modest change will trigger an extreme chain of consequences, which is a slippery slope.
questions.topic: Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The old bridge stood like a giant stone arch above the river,' which literary device is used?
questions.explanation: The sentence compares the bridge to a stone arch using the word like, which makes it a simile.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: In the sentence The hero was reluctant to enter the dark cave after hearing the rumors about its dangers, what does reluctant most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling to do something, which explains the hero's hesitation to enter the cave.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The bells rang silver through the dusk,' which adjective gives the sound a visible quality?
questions.explanation: Silver gives the bells' sound a visible color and quality, so the sentence creates imagery rather than merely describing loudness.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature through Fallacies in Depth

questions.prompt: An argument says, You should not trust my plan for a recycling program because you failed to win a science award in middle school. Which logical fallacy does the argument commit?
questions.explanation: The argument attacks the person's past record instead of addressing the recycling plan, which is an ad hominem attack.
questions.topic: Tester 3 of 9: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9

questions.prompt: Which meaning belongs to the prefix mis- in misfortune?
questions.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrong or bad, as it does in misfortune.
questions.topic: Prefixes and Suffixes

questions.prompt: A student who is terrified of speaking in front of an audience is chosen to give the class presentation. Which type of irony is shown?
questions.explanation: Situational irony occurs when the outcome contrasts with what was expected, as a terrified student is chosen to give a presentation.
questions.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Literary Devices

kept.explanation: Alliteration is the repetition of the same consonant sound at the beginning of successive words.
kept.topic: Sound Devices in Literature

kept.prompt: A teenager spends several evenings patiently showing an elderly neighbor how to use a video-call app, never rushing when the neighbor asks her to repeat a step. Which statement best expresses the theme suggested by this detail?
choices: Patient care can be a meaningful expression of kindness.
Video-call apps are designed mainly to replace in-person visits.
Older adults should be encouraged to avoid unfamiliar technology.
Teenagers are usually more responsible than older adults.
kept.explanation: The teenager's patient, repeated help presents kindness as care expressed through time and attention.
kept.skill: Identifying Theme from a Literary Detail
kept.topic: Theme in Literature

kept.prompt: An argument says, 'The school must either cancel every arts program or risk losing the community's support.' Which logical fallacy does the argument commit?
kept.explanation: The argument falsely reduces the available choices to canceling all arts programs or losing community support.
kept.topic: Fallacies in Depth

kept.prompt: Which sentence contains an understatement?
choices: The flood reached our first-floor windows with a hungry roar.
The flood reached our first-floor windows, which was a minor inconvenience.
The flood reached our first-floor windows before dawn.
The flood reached our first-floor windows in a dazzling silver sheet.
kept.explanation: Calling a first-floor flood a minor inconvenience deliberately downplays how serious the event is.
kept.topic: Literary Devices

kept.prompt: In the sentence The hero was reluctant to enter the dark cave after hearing the rumors about its dangers, what does reluctant most nearly mean?
kept.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling to do something, which explains the hero's hesitation to enter the cave.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Vocabulary from Literature

kept.prompt: In the word readable, what meaning does the suffix -able contribute?
choices: not yet able to be read
kept.explanation: The suffix -able means capable of being, so -able in readable means capable of being read.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Word Parts

kept.prompt: A student who is terrified of speaking in front of an audience is chosen to give the class presentation. Which type of irony is shown?
kept.explanation: Situational irony occurs when the outcome contrasts with what was expected, as a terrified student is chosen to give a presentation.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Literary Devices

kept.prompt: Which point of view narrates a story with pronouns such as I, me, and my?
kept.explanation: First-person point of view uses pronouns such as I, me, and my to narrate events from a participant's perspective.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Narrative Point of View

kept.prompt: A narrator describes a long-empty school gym as a cathedral of vanished cheers, making the building seem grand but painfully quiet. Which tone is best?
kept.explanation: The phrase vanished cheers and the description of painful quiet create a melancholy, reflective mood.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Tone in Literature

kept.prompt: An advertisement says a supplement is effective because a famous athlete uses it, but gives no research about the supplement. Which logical fallacy does the advertisement commit?
kept.explanation: The argument is an appeal to authority because it treats the athlete's fame and endorsement as proof instead of providing evidence about the supplement.
kept.topic: Entry Check, Part 3 of 9: Fallacies in Depth

kept.prompt: In a novel Sam read, the order of events was so ____ that he reread the chapter three times and still could not identify the first major change. Which word best completes the sentence?
kept.explanation: Convoluted means complex and difficult to understand, which matches Sam's inability to follow the sequence of events.
kept.topic: Tester 3 of 9:

kept.prompt: The narrator calls the abandoned garden a wilderness of weeds and tangled vines. Which word best explains wilderness in this context?
choices: a modest place with few visitors
kept.explanation: Here, wilderness describes an overgrown place where plants grow without order or care.
kept.topic: Vocabulary from Literature

kept.prompt: Which meaning belongs to the prefix mis- in misfortune?
kept.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrong or bad, as it does in misfortune.
kept.topic: Prefixes and Suffixes

rejected.prompt: A narrator writes, 'Her voice stayed steady, though her fingers tightened around the cup.' Which inference is best supported by this description?
choices: The character is angry with everyone in the room.
The character has forgotten what she planned to say.
The character is trying to appear calm while she feels nervous.
The character is completely relaxed and enjoying the moment.
rejected.explanation: The steady voice and tightened fingers together suggest that the character is controlling her nerves rather than feeling relaxed.
rejected.reason: explanation-key: the explanation describes option 4 (score 1.00) more than the keyed option 3 (score 0.00)

rejected.prompt: Identify the line that uses an oxymoron.
choices: The rain fell softly all night.
The team won the difficult match.
The old road climbed gently uphill.
rejected.explanation: Freezing fire joins contradictory temperature ideas in adjacent words, making the line an oxymoron.

rejected.prompt: After a character receives a letter, he reads it twice, slips it into a drawer, and avoids mentioning it. What does this behavior most strongly suggest?
choices: The letter has emotional significance for him.
The letter was written in a foreign language.
He plans to use the drawer for storage.
He has received many letters that day.
rejected.explanation: Reading the letter twice, hiding it away, and avoiding discussion most strongly suggest that it carries emotional significance.

rejected.prompt: A story follows two former rivals who exchange letters about a damaged bridge, gradually repair it together, and remain friends after the work ends. What message does the story's development most clearly convey?
choices: Competition is the strongest force in every relationship.
A damaged object cannot be repaired without public attention.
Friendship ends when practical work is completed.
Cooperation can turn conflict into lasting connection.
rejected.explanation: The rivals repair the bridge through cooperation and remain friends afterward, showing how shared work can create lasting connection.

rejected.prompt: What is the name of the reasoning error in this statement: No one has shown that this diet prevents illness, so it cannot prevent illness?
rejected.explanation: The argument treats the absence of proof against the diet as proof that it cannot work, which is an argument from ignorance.

rejected.prompt: In the sentence 'The ephemeral rainbow vanished as the sun moved on,' what does ephemeral mean?
choices: lasting for a very short time
lasting for a very long time
changing from one color to another
rejected.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time, which matches the rainbow's quick disappearance in the sentence.

rejected.prompt: A candidate argues against a longer lunch period by describing how inconvenient the school parking lot is, although parking has no bearing on the lunch-period proposal. Which reasoning error does this argument commit?
rejected.explanation: The parking lot is unrelated to the lunch-period proposal, so discussing it distracts from the issue rather than supporting the candidate's claim.
